chunks: And from him (Al-Hadith) from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who undergoes cupping, so he said: 'There is no harm, unless he fears weakness in his own self.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is cupping permissible for a fasting person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that cupping does not inherently break the fast, distinguishing between the act itself and its physiological effect on the fasting individual. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that *hijamah* is only considered *mukrah* (disliked) or potentially nullifying if it leads to significant weakness (*da'f*) that impairs the worshipper, rather than being automatically voiding like eating or drinking. This highlights the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding medical treatments during Ramadan, prioritizing the preservation of health and worship capacity.
